issues.description: Field visibility for Lecture attributes differs between artifacts. In the problem statement UML (lines 63-68) the Lecture attributes are shown as private (prefixed with '-'). The solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java, lines 6-10) declares the five attributes (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) as private. The template (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java, lines 4-5) currently exposes two attributes as public (public String lectureName; public int numberOfInscribedStudents;) and does not declare the other three attributes. This discrepancy may confuse students about the intended encapsulation (whether fields should be public or private) and whether they must implement getters/setters or change field visibility.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's field declarations match the UML and the solution by declaring the lecture attributes as private. Specifically, in template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java replace the public declarations with private declarations and add the missing attributes: private String lectureName; private int numberOfInscribedStudents; private int numberOfGuestStudents; private int numberOfLecturers; private int numberOfTutors;. Leave method TODOs (constructor/getters/setters/etc.) for students to implement so the pedagogical intent is preserved.
